nodes.label: Proxmox credential discovery

nodes.label: In-memory Proxmox credentials cache
nodes.rationale: The operator keeps a normalized-URL to credentials map in memory so each VM operation is an O(1) lookup with no external credential store.

nodes.label: Multi-Instance Architecture
nodes.rationale: One operator Deployment manages many Proxmox instances. Helm writes one Secret and one set of PROXMOX_<INSTANCE>_ env vars per instance. Handlers resolve credentials at VM operation time.

nodes.label: Proxmox URL normalization
nodes.rationale: _normalize_url strips the scheme and trailing slash, lowercases the host, and adds default port 8006. Lookup tries an exact normalized match, then a hostname-only match.

nodes.label: status.lastHook
nodes.rationale: Feedback is status.lastHook with operation, state, ranAt, message, and jobName, plus a Kubernetes Event and Job logs scraped by Alloy. CRDs must include spec.hooks and status.lastHook before the backend embeds scripts, because unknown fields are pruned.

nodes.label: Multi-instance Proxmox configuration
nodes.rationale: proxmox.instances in Helm values lists URL, username, and API token per cluster. A ProxmoxVM does not carry proxmoxUrl. On the platform cluster, install CRDs before creating Proxmox objects.

nodes.label: Per-instance Proxmox Secrets
nodes.rationale: Helm creates proxmox-credentials-<id> for each instance. Keys are PROXMOX_URL, PROXMOX_USERNAME, PROXMOX_TOKEN_ID, and PROXMOX_TOKEN_SECRET. Instance ids become env var segments by uppercasing and replacing hyphens with underscores.

nodes.label: ProxmoxNodeRef credential selection
nodes.rationale: The operator reads spec.proxmoxNodeRef.name, loads that ProxmoxNode in the same namespace, and matches spec.proxmoxUrl against configured instances. ProxmoxNode also owns maintenanceMode.

nodes.label: Proxmox URL matching
nodes.rationale: Matching is exact on the normalized URL, then hostname-only if the port is omitted. Comparison is case-insensitive and protocol-agnostic, and port 8006 is the default.

nodes.label: Kept multi-instance docs
nodes.rationale: MULTI_INSTANCE.md and ARCHITECTURE_MULTI_INSTANCE.md were kept on purpose while obsolete backup and snapshot design notes were deleted. samples/proxmoxvm.yaml comments were aligned with real OperationType values.

nodes.label: Kept VM operation types
nodes.rationale: Operation types that remain are created, started, stopped, deleted, restarted, and reinstalled. Pause and reboot are not operation types. SnapshotPhase.DISABLED and VM_STATUS_PAUSED were removed.

nodes.label: CustomResourceDefinition solusvmvms.vm.solusvm.com
nodes.rationale: SolusVMVM requires solusvmNodeRef so the VM names a SolusVMNode instead of embedding a panel URL. spec.operation.requestedAt is unique per apply so Restart, start, and stop re-run while type is unchanged, because an identical spec does not bump generation and Liqo re-fires kopf on.create. spec.hooks holds provider lifecycle scripts keyed by operation.

nodes.label: CustomResourceDefinition solusvmvncrequests.vm.solusvm.com
nodes.rationale: A SolusVMVNCRequest names a SolusVMVM via spec.vmRef and returns a noVNC websocket URL plus the VNC password. ttl bounds the ticket-fetch window (default 30 seconds).

nodes.label: ClusterRole solusvm-operator-role
nodes.rationale: The operator may fully reconcile solusvmvms and solusvmvncrequests, but may only get, list, watch, and patch solusvmcontrols and solusvmnodes. It can also manage Secrets and batch Jobs used by hooks.

nodes.label: CustomResourceDefinition virtfusioncontrols.vm.virtfusion.com
nodes.rationale: VirtFusionControl stores the control panel URL in spec.endpoint. Status lists discovered hypervisors, including group id, capacity, maintenance, and IP.

nodes.label: CustomResourceDefinition virtfusionnodes.vm.virtfusion.com
nodes.rationale: hypervisorGroupId is sent as hypervisorId in POST /servers. controlRef names the VirtFusionControl. When maintenanceMode is enabled, reconciliation skips state checks.

nodes.label: CustomResourceDefinition virtfusionvms.vm.virtfusion.com
nodes.rationale: VirtFusionVM requires virtfusionNodeRef, packageId, operatingSystemId, and userExtRelationId. ipv4 is empty on create so VirtFusion assigns from its IP block. blockOutboundSmtp attaches the first firewall ruleset whose name contains smtp, independent of NodeRings guest firewall APIs. requestedAt re-runs power operations without a generation bump because Liqo re-fires kopf on.create.

nodes.label: CustomResourceDefinition virtfusionvncrequests.vm.virtfusion.com
nodes.rationale: VirtFusionVNCRequest names a VirtFusionVM via spec.vmRef. Status returns the hypervisor management IP, an RFB TCP port, and an RFB password rather than a noVNC websocket URL.

nodes.label: ClusterRole virtfusion-operator-role
nodes.rationale: Full reconcile rights on virtfusionvms and virtfusionvncrequests. virtfusioncontrols and virtfusionnodes are limited to get, list, watch, and patch. Secrets and batch Jobs are included for credentials and hook Jobs.

nodes.label: FirewallRuleSet example-web-firewall
nodes.rationale: Sample ingress accept rule for TCP 80 and 443 to a single IPv4 and IPv6 address, from anywhere, at position 0.

nodes.label: ProxmoxVM demo-vm8
nodes.rationale: A companion ProxmoxNode in the same namespace owns the Proxmox endpoint. ProxmoxVM never carries proxmoxUrl. blockOutboundSmtp is independent of firewallRuleSet. Allocated VMID is written to status.vmId and is not patched back into spec. Operation types are created, started, stopped, restarted, reinstalled, and deleted.

nodes.label: Per-instance credential isolation
nodes.rationale: Each Proxmox instance has its own Secret. Credentials are never shared, API tokens are preferred over passwords, and each instance can be rotated independently. Missing credentials or connection failures set the VM phase to Error.

nodes.label: ProxmoxNode endpoint source of truth
nodes.rationale: Diagrams that put proxmoxUrl on each ProxmoxVM are outdated. ProxmoxVM uses spec.proxmoxNodeRef.name, and the operator reads proxmoxUrl from the linked ProxmoxNode so the node is the single source of truth.

nodes.label: Unused operator code removal
nodes.rationale: High-confidence dead code and obsolete backup and snapshot design notes were removed. Live reconcile handlers, CRDs, chart RBAC, and status models such as ProxmoxVMStatus were left untouched.

nodes.label: VirtFusion control-plane instances
nodes.rationale: Agent installs never verify the control-plane TLS certificate. Tokens stay in the Secret applied with kubectl, not Helm --set. userApiToken, userId, and userName are written by nr cluster register.

nodes.label: At-most-once hook Jobs
nodes.rationale: Job name is hook- plus the first 16 hex chars of sha1 of namespace, name, operation, and generation. AlreadyExists means the hook already ran. reinstall and reinstalled both use the reinstalled script. HOOKS_MAX_CONCURRENT defaults to 5. The script Secret is owned by the Job and the default TTL is 24 hours.

nodes.label: Provider lifecycle hook scripts
nodes.rationale: After a successful VM operation the operator runs a provider Python script as an isolated Job. Hook failure never fails the VM operation. Jobs are never executed inside the operator process. If the VM operation is skipped as already handled, the hook does not fire.

nodes.label: Provider hook Secret
nodes.rationale: Providers who need credentials inside the Job, without storing them on the platform, create noderings-hook-secrets in the hooks namespace. Keys are injected as env and as files under /var/run/secrets/noderings-hooks. A missing Secret does not fail the Job. Explicit NODERINGS_* env vars win over Secret keys of the same name. The control plane stores the script source. The Job Secret is the cluster-side copy.

nodes.label: Deployment solusvm-operator
nodes.rationale: The operator container runs kopf run -A -m solusvm_operator.handlers. HOOKS_JOB_NAMESPACE is the dedicated hook namespace so hook Jobs are not created beside the operator.

nodes.label: Namespace solusvm-operator hook jobs
nodes.rationale: Hook Jobs get their own namespace, labeled noderings.com/hook-jobs and pinned to the release namespace, with pod security enforce, audit, and warn set to restricted.

nodes.label: NetworkPolicy solusvm-operator-hook-jobs
nodes.rationale: Hook pods may egress to public TCP 80 and 443 except RFC1918, link-local, CGNAT, loopback, and multicast, to kube-dns in kube-system, and to optional privateEgress and extraEgress CIDRs.

nodes.label: NetworkPolicy solusvm-operator-operator
nodes.rationale: The operator pod may egress only to TCP 443, the Kubernetes API on 6443, and DNS on 53.

nodes.label: Deployment virtfusion-operator
nodes.rationale: The operator runs kopf run -A -m virtfusion_operator.handlers. Each virtfusion.instances entry injects URL, token, and optional user API token, user id, and user name from a credentials Secret. HOOKS_JOB_NAMESPACE points at the hook namespace.

nodes.label: Namespace virtfusion-operator hook jobs
nodes.rationale: Hook Jobs run in the namespace from virtfusion-operator.hookNamespace, separate from VM CRs and hypervisor credential Secrets.

nodes.label: NetworkPolicy virtfusion-operator-hook-jobs
nodes.rationale: Selects pods labeled noderings.com/hook-runner. Egress allows public TCP 80 and 443 except private, link-local, CGNAT, loopback, and multicast ranges, DNS only to kube-dns, plus hooks.privateEgress and hooks.extraEgress.

nodes.label: NetworkPolicy virtfusion-operator-operator
nodes.rationale: Operator egress is TCP 443, Kubernetes API 6443, and DNS.

nodes.label: VirtFusion lifecycle hook Jobs
nodes.rationale: Hooks require a CNI that enforces NetworkPolicy. An empty jobNamespace becomes {Release.Namespace}-hooks so Jobs and script Secrets are not beside VM CRs or hypervisor credential Secrets. providerSecretName defaults to noderings-hook-secrets and is optional so a missing Secret does not fail Jobs. An empty image uses the operator image, which has stdlib Python.

nodes.label: Hook privateEgress exceptions
nodes.rationale: except CIDRs must be subsets of cidr. Cluster, docker, kind, metadata, and loopback stay blocked via except plus the public deny-list, while provider LAN and Tailscale remain reachable.

nodes.label: Hook job namespace
nodes.rationale: Hook Jobs and script Secrets run in {Release.Namespace}-hooks, overridable with hooks.jobNamespace, so VM CRs and hypervisor credential Secrets stay in the operator namespace. Do not enable hooks on a CNI that ignores NetworkPolicy, or hook pods would have unrestricted egress.

nodes.label: SSRF-hardened hook egress
nodes.rationale: Default egress is public TCP 80 and 443 except RFC1918, link-local including cloud metadata, CGNAT, loopback, and multicast, plus IPv6 public space except ULA and link-local. Provider private ranges are allowed except Kubernetes, docker, and kind CIDRs. DNS is only kube-dns in kube-system. Jobs have no service account token, no hypervisor credentials, and stdlib-only Python.

Do not bake a lab address into the chart, CRD, or image. alloy.configMap.create is false and the name is operator-virtfusion-operator-alloy-config so the subchart consumes the operator ConfigMap.

nodes.label: Pterodactyl Application API
nodes.rationale: Base path is {panel}/api/application. It builds the game catalog, picks allocations, reads Wings configuration, orders servers, and suspends or deletes them. external_id is NR- plus the NodeRings game server uuid.

nodes.label: Pterodactyl application key
nodes.rationale: The application key is sent as Authorization Bearer and is used to create and delete servers, nests, eggs, and nodes, and to suspend.

nodes.label: Pterodactyl Client API
nodes.rationale: Base path is {panel}/api/client. Power signals are start, stop, restart, and kill. File paths stay inside the server root and .. is rejected before the call. On panel 1.15 the database password is nested under attributes.relationships.password.

nodes.label: Pterodactyl client key
nodes.rationale: The client key is what a server owner uses: power, files, schedules, backups, databases, and network. {identifier} is the short client-API id, not the numeric server id.

nodes.label: Pterodactyl create server body
nodes.rationale: POST /servers sends egg startup, docker image, and environment. limits.threads is sent only for a dedicated-CPU plan. An empty environment override does not wipe a non-empty egg default. Memory, swap, and disk are MiB. CPU percent 100 is one core.

nodes.label: Pterodactyl list pagination
nodes.rationale: List endpoints the operator pages through must return meta.pagination.total_pages, page, and per_page. Each row is an attributes object. The exporter server list currently reads page 1 only.

nodes.label: Pterodactyl panel contract
nodes.rationale: This is the panel contract the operator and the metrics exporter use. A legacy panel must keep these endpoints, bodies, and response shapes. NodeRings does not call the panel from the API process. The operator on the provider cluster does, using two keys from the operator Secret. Every request sends Accept application/vnd.pterodactyl.v1+json. NodeRings does not create panel users.

nodes.label: Pterodactyl websocket console
nodes.rationale: GET /servers/{id}/websocket returns token and socket, and the browser never sees that response. The operator opens the Wings socket, sends an auth event, then send logs. Customer commands are forwarded as Wings events. POST /servers/{id}/command is not used.

nodes.label: Wings daemon API
nodes.rationale: Wings lives at scheme://fqdn:daemon_listen, not on the panel. Dedicated CPU reads cpu_count from GET /api/system. File transfer uses the signed URL with no panel key.

nodes.label: Wings node token
nodes.rationale: GET /api/system on the Wings daemon uses the node token. If Bearer token returns 401 or 403, the operator retries Bearer token_id.token.

nodes.label: Deployment solusvm-operator-exporter

nodes.label: Deployment solusvm-operator-vnc-gateway

nodes.label: NetworkPolicy solusvm-operator-vnc-gateway

nodes.label: Service vnc-gateway
